            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: A stable identifier shared by owners that belong to the same household.
                The household is keyed on (lastName, postcode) and is the first 12 hex characters of
                the SHA-256 digest over the normalized lastName (case-insensitive, collapsed
                whitespace) joined to the postcode by '|', so any two owners sharing a lastName and
                postcode automatically receive the same value. Absent for owners without a postcode,
                which belong to no shared household.
              type: string
              example: '3F2A1B0C9D8E'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: The owner's derived identity key, formed as
                '<telephone>|<email>|<householdId>' where telephone is the normalized E.164
                telephone, email is the lower-cased email (empty when the owner has no email)
                and householdId is the shared household identifier (empty when the owner shares
                no household). Hard duplicate detection is keyed on the household, so two owners
                sharing a lastName and postcode are the same household, and a second such owner
                is rejected with 409 Conflict unless it sets sharesHousehold.

The picture is now clear. Key findings:

- The **only test class in the project is `AcceptanceTest`**, and it is the *pending change's* spec — it asserts `$.membershipPoints` (value 3) and `membershipLevel` (value 2). It fails today because `membershipPoints` does not exist yet. There are no other tests, so there is no currently-passing regression suite to protect beyond "don't break compilation/behavior."
- Implementing the points system to turn that test green is explicitly out of scope for this step, so `AcceptanceTest` stays red by design until the change lands.

## What I restructured (behavior-preserving)

The two hotspots (`getMembershipPoints`, which the change adds, and `getMembershipLevel`, which it rewrites) would each have to inline the same null-guarded factor checks. This codebase's established idiom is exactly the opposite: each derivation is a `public static` "single definition" resolver over raw values, with an instance getter delegating to it (see `countryCodeOf`, `regionForPostcode`, `nationalNumberLength`, …).

So in `Owner.java` I extracted the three membership factors that already exist today into that same shape:

- `hasEmail(String)` — the single definition of email presence
- `hasNoNamesakes(Integer)` — the "no namesakes" factor
- `hasLongTenure(LocalDate, LocalDate)` — the "tenure over 365 days" factor (pure, takes `asOf` so it stays testable, matching how the other static resolvers take raw args)

`getMembershipLevel` now delegates to these; its arithmetic and documented contract are unchanged.

I also pointed `OwnerMapper.contactPreference` at `Owner.hasEmail(...)`, removing the duplicated email-presence check so the "single definition" claim actually holds.

Why this makes the upcoming change natural: the future `getMembershipPoints` reuses `hasEmail`/`hasNoNamesakes`/`hasLongTenure` and adds one sibling factor (large household) in the same idiom; the future `getMembershipLevel` collapses to a one-line `membershipLevelForPoints(getMembershipPoints())`, with the points→level band table added as another static resolver — the maintainer's natural home for it.

## Verification

- `./mvnw -o test` compiles cleanly (main + MapStruct annotation processing + tests all build).
- Behavior is preserved: each extraction is a literal move of the existing expression (a single `LocalDate.now()` captured once, as before).
- The **only** failing test is the pre-existing `AcceptanceTest.coreReturnsPointsAndLevel` — same failure as before my changes (`No value at JSON path "$.membershipPoints"`), which the upcoming feature will resolve. No new failures were introduced.

I did **not** implement the points system, per the instructions.
